questions.stem: Which of the following is a major source of water pollution?

options.text: Solar panels
Agricultural fertilisers and sewage
Recycling centres
Wind turbines

questions.explanation: Agricultural fertilisers and sewage are major sources of water pollution. When they enter waterways, they can cause eutrophication and contaminate drinking water supplies.

options.text: The excessive growth of algae in water caused by nutrient pollution, which depletes oxygen and kills aquatic life
The process of cleaning polluted water
The natural filtering of water through rocks
The evaporation of polluted water

questions.explanation: Eutrophication occurs when excess nutrients (often from fertilisers) enter water, causing rapid algal growth (algal bloom). When the algae die, decomposing bacteria use up the dissolved oxygen, suffocating fish and other aquatic organisms.

questions.stem: How can toxic chemicals from industrial waste affect aquatic ecosystems?

options.text: They can accumulate in the food chain (bioaccumulation) and poison organisms at higher levels
They make the water cleaner
They evaporate harmlessly from the water
They only affect plants, not animals

questions.explanation: Toxic chemicals such as heavy metals can bioaccumulate in organisms and become more concentrated as they pass up the food chain. This can cause poisoning and death in predators at the top of the food chain.

questions.stem: What happens when untreated sewage enters a river?

options.text: Bacteria decompose the sewage, using up dissolved oxygen and reducing the oxygen available for fish
It makes the river flow faster
It makes the river water more acidic permanently
It has no effect on the river ecosystem

questions.explanation: Bacteria decompose the organic matter in sewage, consuming large amounts of dissolved oxygen in the process. This reduces the oxygen available for fish and other aquatic organisms, potentially killing them.

questions.stem: Which type of water pollutant can come from pesticides used in farming?

options.text: Radioactive waste
Toxic organic chemicals that can poison wildlife and contaminate drinking water
Heavy metals only
Carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Pesticides are toxic organic chemicals designed to kill pests. When they are washed into waterways by rain (run-off), they can poison aquatic organisms and contaminate drinking water supplies.

questions.stem: Why is it important to treat water before it is safe to drink?

options.text: To make the water warmer
To remove harmful microorganisms, dissolved chemicals, and particulates that could cause disease
To add flavour to the water
To remove all the minerals from the water

questions.explanation: Water treatment removes harmful bacteria, viruses, dissolved pollutants, and suspended particles. Processes like filtration, sedimentation, and chlorination ensure the water is safe to drink.

questions.stem: How can farmers help reduce water pollution from their land?

options.text: By removing all vegetation near rivers
By irrigating fields with seawater
By applying fertilisers carefully, using buffer zones near waterways, and storing manure properly
By using more fertiliser to grow crops faster

questions.explanation: Farmers can reduce water pollution by applying the correct amount of fertiliser at the right time, maintaining buffer strips of vegetation near waterways to trap run-off, and storing manure properly to prevent it leaching into water.
